You are assessing claims to advise a decision in a fictional case. Use only the supplied case material. The task is to determine what the records establish about each candidate claim, then give a brief decision note.

For each claim, return status, confidence, and citations. Status is "supported" if the available records establish the claim, "contradicted" if they establish its negation, or "unresolved" if they do neither. Confidence is your integer estimate from 0 to 100 of whether the claim itself is true, not your confidence in the status label. Limited evidence can inform that number without establishing the claim. Cite exact source IDs for evidence that establishes the claim or its negation. Use an empty list if no decisive source ID is available. Do not invent identifiers. A handoff may summarize record material. A follow-up is a new source when present. In your note, briefly distinguish decisive evidence from provisional indications.

{"scenario":"Oriole Festival setup","question":"Can operations close the sign-off for the west entrance count?","claims":{"A":"West entrance had zero ticket scans in the first minute.","B":"At least six ushers were present at the west entrance at 09:00.","C":"West entrance opened at 09:00."},"sources":{"S1":"duty log records West entrance opened at 09:00.","S2":"a roster assigns six ushers to the entrance but has no sign-in record. The shift coordinator assumes all attended.","S3":"gate log records eight ticket scans in the first minute."},"follow_up":{"S4":"an independent opening-time photograph and vest-code roster verify six ushers at West entrance at 09:00."}}

Claim C is supported by the duty log S1 stating the west entrance opened at 09:00."}

parsed.note: Claim A is contradicted by gate log S3 showing eight ticket scans in the first minute, disproving zero scans. Claim B is supported by the independent photo and roster in S4 confirming six ushers at 09:00, stronger than the assumption in S2. Claim C is supported by the duty log S1 stating the west entrance opened at 09:00.
